clue.text: Master criminal better kept in solitary

indicators.note: something kept in another thing sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: solitary means on one's own
to cap a story is to better it

explanation.surface: A gangster boss ends up in solitary confinement, where he is better off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective but is the verb: to cap something is to outdo it. It sits inside ALONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era, a byword for criminal mastermind.

clue.text: A player confused about end of overture, such as 1812

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the extra letter is taken in
the end of a word is its last letter, the one added here
confused means muddled, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A musician gets muddled near the end of Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture.
explanation.walkthrough: 1812 suggests the overture, but it is just a year; 1812 divides by four.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap year has 366 days and falls every fourth year; 1812 is divisible by four, so it was one.

clue.text: Spoke disparagingly — steered clear of including corrupt admin

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to avert is to turn aside or avoid

indicators.note: corrupt means altered from its proper form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains bitterly about a crooked administration they have kept away from.
explanation.definitionFit: To animadvert is to pass critical comment, so animadverted means made censorious remarks.

clue.text: Not in clique, for start

parts.note: not in means out
a set is a social group or clique

explanation.surface: Being outside the in-crowd is the starting point.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset is the beginning of an undertaking, as in 'from the outset'.

clue.text: What one faces, coming from West Indians' part of world

definitions.text: What one faces, coming from West
definitions.meaning: first meaning: travelling from the west, you look towards the opposite direction
second meaning: the region of ... Indians, the Orient

explanation.walkthrough: 'West Indians' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits after West; the Indians are East Indians.
explanation.definitionFit: The compass point opposite west is what a traveller from the west faces, and it names the Orient, home of the East Indies.

clue.text: Page or display of data easily moved

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
taken as written
a table sets data out in rows and columns

explanation.surface: A page or a chart of figures can be shifted without trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable means light or compact enough to be carried about.

clue.text: Missing target I had in partnership

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a partnership speaks of itself as we
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: I missed the mark while batting in a partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a wide is a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide means off target, as a shot or ball that passes to one side of what was aimed at.

clue.text: Doctor stayed with multinational organization, initially, not firm

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so this abbreviation goes first

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic remained with an international body at first, though wavering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsteady means shaky or liable to wobble, the opposite of firm.

clue.text: A peculiar point about party raising issue for others

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something peculiar is odd and out of the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An odd point is raised concerning a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumble takes in the party as well as the point; 'issue' means offspring, not a topic for debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is bringing up a child born to other parents, a cryptic sense of raising someone else's issue, issue meaning offspring.

clue.text: Somalian's heart is elsewhere in Africa

indicators.note: a heart is the centre of something, so only the central letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the four letters at the centre of the word

explanation.surface: A Somali is homesick, his heart in some other part of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Somalia is in Africa, so 'elsewhere in Africa' points to another African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a West African country, far from Somalia in the east, so it is somewhere else on the continent.

clue.text: Art patron's daughter joining chaps ahead of time? It's not true

indicators.note: ahead of means placed in front, fixing the order of the final two parts

parts.note: a daughter is a miss, a young unmarried woman
Henry Tate, the sugar magnate who founded London's Tate gallery
chaps are men
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A wealthy art collector's daughter arrives with some men too early, or so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Art patron's daughter' as Miss Tate; Henry Tate founded the Tate gallery in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstatement is a false or inaccurate assertion, something said that is not true.

clue.text: How attraction may happen in delightful way, securing catch

indicators.note: securing means holding something fast, so one word grips the other inside it

parts.note: delightfully, as if by magic
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: Romance blossoms wonderfully when someone makes a good catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attraction' suggests romance, but it is the physical pull of a magnet.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnets attract iron, so attraction may happen by magnetic force, an adverb matching 'how'.

clue.text: Disorder at event including Democrat prolonged dispute

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so the abbreviation joins the letters
disorder means a lack of proper arrangement, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: Trouble at a political event involving a Democrat turns into a long-running feud.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long feud, originally a blood feud between families, so a dispute that goes on and on.

clue.text: One person directing what students will learn in the future

parts.note: a means one

parts.words: person directing what students will learn
parts.note: a head teacher runs the school and its curriculum

explanation.surface: A single teacher decides what pupils will study in time to come.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, the head is the head teacher, the principal of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead means forthcoming, still to come, as in 'the years ahead'.

clue.text: Capital got constricted in South America?

indicators.note: something constricted is squeezed by what wraps round it, so one word is held inside another

parts.note: the boa, a snake that squeezes its prey, lives in South America
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about a capital city that got hemmed in somewhere in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constricted' does double duty: it puts GOT inside and, with the South American hint, conjures the boa constrictor doing the squeezing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogota is the capital city of Colombia, which is itself in South America.

clue.text: Cheese ready for case? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling a little short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a barrister's brief is what makes them ready for a court case

explanation.surface: Is a cheese ripe enough to go in a display case? Almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a cheese box, but it is a legal case, and a brief is a lawyer's instructions for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cow's-milk cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: Part of defence worker used for action in court

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football or hockey
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A defence lawyer's assistant is put to work on a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence' and 'court' suggest the law, but they are sport: a back defends, and the court is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhand is a tennis stroke played with the back of the hand facing the ball, a move on the court.

clue.text: Bishop, perhaps, making calm pronouncement

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so we go by the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: calm is peace, which is said the same way as the answer

explanation.surface: A bishop delivers a soothing statement from the pulpit.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop is not a cleric but a chessman; 'perhaps' warns that it is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a bishop is one of the pieces, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Heap of burning stuff spotted after turning over range

indicators.note: after means following, setting which piece comes second

parts.note: a pyre is a pile of material for burning, as for a funeral

indicators.note: turning over flips the word end to end, so it is read backwards

parts.note: spotted means seen

explanation.surface: A bonfire is spotted after a vehicle turns over on the cooking range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are the mountain range dividing France from Spain.

clue.text: Crime people want to commit

parts.note: surface reading: an offence people are keen to carry out; setter's reading: a sin committed by wanting what other people have

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crime' stretches to sin, and 'want' is not desire to commit it but the wanting itself, coveting another's goods, that is the offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy, one of the seven deadly sins, is resentful longing for what someone else possesses, so wanting is how it is committed.

clue.text: Local in country pub has unfinished nasty drink

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking its ending, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: nasty means vile
lager is a drink

explanation.surface: A regular at a rural inn has half finished a horrible drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's nearby pub; here local is a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A villager is a resident, a local, of a village, the sort found drinking in a country pub.

clue.text: Small sailing ship, say, east of Cape

indicators.note: in an across answer, east of means to the right of, so this part follows the other

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: A little sailing vessel is spotted, let's say, east of a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb utter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutter is a small single-masted sailing boat, often used by coastguards or for carrying messages.

clue.text: Follower's record that is holding another back

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: holding means gripping something inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so the second record is read from right to left

parts.note: another record, an LP or long-player

explanation.surface: A fan's record, it seems, is holding up another one.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower of a teacher or leader, as the apostles followed Jesus.

clue.text: Foreign woman's negative response second time around

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the response sits inside

parts.note: an era is a period of time
the word for refusal

explanation.surface: A woman abroad says no for the second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Señora is the Spanish title for a married woman, so a woman from abroad.

clue.text: Something seen in Copenhagen — Danes' ulterior motive

parts.note: something visible only inside other words is concealed there
the letters run across the end of the city and the start of its people

explanation.surface: Something spotted in Copenhagen reveals what the Danes are secretly up to.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes itself: the second word is concealed in 'Copenhagen Danes', so it is a hidden one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden agenda is a secret plan or purpose concealed behind an apparent one, the same as an ulterior motive.

clue.text: Tie up and cut off weed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: moor a ship at a quay
second meaning: shorten, as a tail or wages
third meaning: a broad-leaved plant of the sorrel family

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two: the gardening surface hides a nautical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers mooring a vessel, docking a tail or pay, and the coarse weed whose leaves soothe nettle stings.

clue.text: Suit, for example, in card game, turned over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: brag is an old British card game, a forerunner of poker

explanation.surface: A suit of cards is flipped face up during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' and 'card game' point to cards, but the suit is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing or dress, and a suit is one example of it.

clue.text: Circle added to section of plane, for instance, as emblem

indicators.note: added to means attached after something, setting the order of the two parts

parts.note: a plane is a tree, and a cut section of its trunk is a log
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: A ring is painted on part of an aircraft as an insignia.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane is not an aircraft but the plane tree, common in London streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is a company's or group's identifying symbol, so an emblem.

clue.text: Knew race must be rearranged? Ascot, it could be

indicators.note: rearranged plainly says the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who knew the race result wants it rerun — at Ascot, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is the famous Royal Ascot racecourse, which the race suggests, but an ascot is also a broad cravat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a wide formal tie or cravat worn round the throat, an example of neckwear.

clue.text: Seaside facility at end of quay embraced by business leaders

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside another's arms, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: a company's board of directors

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is taken here

parts.note: taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Company directors take over a seaside amenity at the end of the quay.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatyard is a place by the water where boats are built, repaired or stored.
